events.description: Can you turn your imagination into the perfect prompt? In the AI Prompt Battle, participants will be challenged to recreate a given reference image using only the power of AI prompting. Each participant will receive an image and must craft a detailed and effective prompt to generate an output that matches the original image as closely as possible. Test your creativity, observation skills, and prompt-engineering abilities as you compete to create the closest visual match. The participant whose AI-generated image most accurately resembles the reference image will emerge victorious!
rules: 24 Teams Only

Internet access will be provided by the organizers
AI Tools will be provided on the spot by the organizers
No smart phones, smart watches, etc. allowed in the lab while you are participating for the event.
No external help from, faculty, or online communities
Copying another participant's prompt or image is strictly prohibited.
Tie-Breaker Rule: If two participants have equal scores: The participant who used a more effective and creative prompt with fewer unnecessary attempts will be declared the winner.

events.eventTagline: Find the Bugs. Build the Solution.
events.description:
The event consists of 2 rounds
Round 1: Debugging Round
Participants will be given a code containing errors (syntax, logical, and runtime errors). They must identify and fix all the errors within 15 minutes. The code will be displayed on the projector, and participants will solve it using Notepad. Mobile phones and internet access are strictly prohibited. Any participant who fails to complete the debugging within 15 minutes will be disqualified. Only participants who correctly complete the debugging challenge within the time limit will qualify for the next round.
Round 2: Coding Round
Only the participants selected from the Debugging Round will advance to this round.Participants will be given a programming problem and must write a complete solution within 30 minutes.The program must produce the correct output for the given problem. Time limit for this round is 30 minutes.The first three participants to correctly complete the program and submit it will be declared the winners (1st, 2nd, and 3rd respectively).
rules: 20 Teams Only
Note: Python will be used in both the rounds
Maximum 20 participants will be allowed.
If registrations exceed 20, an elimination process may be conducted before the event.

Participants must follow the instructions of the volunteers and event coordinators at all times.
Any form of plagiarism, unfair means, or misconduct will result in immediate disqualification.
The decision of the event coordinators will be final and binding.
Time limit for this round - 30 minutes.
